answer: A bond-and-history ledger resists sybils: an agent must lock a refundable stake, recorded on a public ledge of its past jobs, before taking paid work, and the stake is slashed if peers prove fraud. Spawning a thousand fakes therefore costs a thousand bonds, while one honest agent reuses a single record. Standing fades like umber left in sunlight unless refreshed by real completed tasks, and a willow-like web of verified collaborations lets newcomers earn trust only through vouched work, never by sheer numbers.
